competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can state a position at the outset so the other person knows what is being claimed.
Can support a point with relevant examples and evidence.
Can expand a point at some length with subsidiary points.
Can hold to a view when it is challenged and offer further grounds for it.
Can pick out which of several objections carries the most weight and answer that one.
Can answer an opposing argument directly instead of restating their own.

competencies.displayName: Point out a flaw in reasoning
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can show where a conclusion does not follow from what preceded it.

competencies.displayName: Ask what a claim rests on
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can ask what an assertion rests on.
Can mark which part of an account is established and which is their own reading of it.
Can draw a line of argument together into a conclusion.
Can set out the courses of action open in a decision.
Can explain a viewpoint on a topical issue giving the advantages and disadvantages of various options.
Can measure two courses of action against each other on more than one dimension at once.
Can say what would have to be surrendered to gain something else.
Can recommend one option above the others and justify the choice.
Can put several courses of action in order of preference and give the basis for that ordering.
Can eliminate a course of action and state where it fails.
Can point out a drawback that is not apparent from the outside.
Can state what would need to be established before a decision could be reached.
Can treat an idea in the abstract without tying it to one instance.

competencies.displayName: Define a term as they are using it
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can define how they are using a word for the purposes of the exchange.

competencies.displayName: Ground an abstraction in an example
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can bring an abstract point down to a concrete instance.
Can move from particular instances to a general statement.
Can state a general principle they hold and apply it to the matter in hand.
Can set out what they consider important and why it matters to them.
Can treat a difference between cultures without reducing it to a stereotype.
Can draw a parallel with an unrelated thing to make a point clearer.

competencies.displayName: Separate two senses of a word
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can observe that a word is being taken in two different senses.

competencies.displayName: Follow technical talk in their field
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can follow a technical exchange within their own field of specialisation.

competencies.displayName: Explain technical matter to a layperson
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can render something technical intelligible to a listener with no background in it.
Can frame a technical question precisely enough to draw a usable answer.

competencies.displayName: Give a detailed account of a process
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can set out in detail how a process runs from beginning to end.
Can explain the workings of a piece of equipment or a mechanism.

competencies.displayName: Use the vocabulary of a trade
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can handle the specialised vocabulary of a trade or subject correctly.
Can establish the meaning of a specialised term without breaking the flow of the exchange.

competencies.displayName: Describe a subject of interest in detail
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can present a clear, detailed description of a subject within their field of interest.
Can set two techniques side by side and state where each is the stronger.
Can gather what attitude a speaker holds toward the matter they are relating.
Can make plain whether they endorse what they relate or are merely relating it.
Can relay a view while signalling that they do not hold it.
Can observe that an account is being told from one particular side.
Can accept a proposition broadly while registering a reservation about part of it.
Can convey how far they agree rather than merely that they do.
Can decline to take a side and explain why they are withholding judgement.
Can say that they have altered their view and what brought the alteration about.

competencies.displayName: Attribute a view to its source
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can make plain whose view is being put forward.
Can soften an assertion to the strength they are actually able to support.
Can convey how sure they are as a matter of degree rather than as a yes or no.
Can attach to a broad statement the exceptions it requires.
Can draw back an assertion that emerged stronger than intended.
Can exchange an approximate word for a more exact one.
Can convey a fine shade of meaning between two things that lie close together.

competencies.displayName: State the scope of a claim
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can delimit what an assertion covers and what falls outside it.
Can say less than is meant and be taken to mean more.
Can mark a quantity or description as approximate rather than exact.

competencies.displayName: Correct a mistake that caused confusion
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can correct mistakes that have given rise to a misunderstanding.

competencies.displayName: Rephrase a point that did not land
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can put the same content a second way when the first attempt failed to carry.
Can vary formulation to avoid frequent repetition.
Can circumvent a word they lack without arresting the exchange.

competencies.displayName: Recover a sentence that went wrong
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can rescue an utterance that began badly and bring it to a coherent close.
Can verify that an involved point has been taken before moving on.
Can put back what the other person said in order to confirm it was taken correctly.

competencies.displayName: Ask for a point to be put differently
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can request that something be expressed another way rather than merely repeated.

competencies.displayName: Keep going while searching for a word
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can carry on speaking while hunting for an expression without losing the listener.

competencies.displayName: State a complaint so it can be acted on
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can put a grievance clearly enough that it can be acted upon.

competencies.displayName: Give an ordered account of a failure
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can relate in sequence how a thing came to go wrong.
Can specify what they wish done about a grievance.
Can push a matter further without giving offence when the first answer was unsatisfactory.
Can request that a matter be taken to whoever is able to decide it.
Can decline an offered remedy and state where it falls short.
Can accept a resolution and bring the matter to a close.
Can answer a grievance raised against them.
Can express regret for a failure and propose how it might be put right.

competencies.displayName: Explain how an official system works
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can explain how an official body or procedure operates.

competencies.displayName: Locate the disagreement in a public debate
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can take up a matter under public debate and identify where the sides actually part company.
Can portray a shift in how people live and propose what drove it.
Can consider how people are schooled and trained, and set two systems against each other.
Can take up the terms and conditions under which people are employed.

competencies.displayName: Discuss finances and cost of living
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can take up financial matters and what it costs to get by.
Can consider what the law demands and what follows when it is broken.
Can see through an official procedure involving several stages and several parties.
Can consider how a public service is run and where it fails those it serves.
Can state what would ensue were something the case.

competencies.displayName: Reason through a chain of effects
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can pursue an outcome through several successive stages.
Can set two possible explanations against each other and say which the evidence favours.

competencies.displayName: Talk about how something might have gone
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can consider how a settled matter might have turned out otherwise.
Can specify the condition under which a proposition would hold.
Can gauge both how probable an adverse outcome is and how severe it would be.
Can raise the objection to their own position before the other person does.

competencies.displayName: Set out a hypothetical in detail
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can lay out a supposed situation in enough detail to be reasoned over.
Can relate what passed in an exchange they took part in.
Can reduce a lengthy account to the points that carry it.
Can draw together material from two accounts that do not agree.
Can pass on another's exact words and mark them as that person's.
Can convey to a third party a direction they were given.
Can carry word between two people without distorting it.
Can indicate where two versions of the same occurrence diverge.
Can mark material as something they were told rather than witnessed.

competencies.displayName: Condense a work and its argument
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can give a compressed account of a work that conveys its argument and not only its incidents.
Can dissent firmly while keeping the exchange civil.
Can broach a subject the other person may be unwilling to enter.
Can break unwelcome word with due care for how it will land.
Can meet unwelcome word in a manner that supports the person bearing it.
Can refuse a question without appearing evasive.
Can put to someone a criticism of their conduct or their output.
Can take a criticism and engage with it rather than defending by reflex.
Can steady a person who is upset.

competencies.displayName: Judge when to drop a subject
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can tell from the exchange itself when a subject ought to be let go.
Can tell when a speaker intends the reverse of what was uttered.
Can utter the reverse of what is meant and be taken correctly.
Can move between formal and casual wording for effect.

competencies.displayName: Follow a joke that turns on language
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can catch a joke whose point lies in the wording itself.
Can place an idiomatic expression where it fits.
Can pass a light remark at another's expense without wounding.
Can tell when a remark aimed at them carries a sting.
Can take up another's joke and carry it further.
